note: Free, keyless historical basemap sources researched for Ground at time of incident. Only sources marked use_in_app true are wired into the picker. Never claim a closer date than the source actually supports.

sources.name: USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection (ImageServer)
sources.coverage_regions: United States, including Puerto Rico; other territories [UNKNOWN] beyond the boxes used in js/period-ground.js
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. Government work). Credit USGS. Requested acknowledgment: Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program.
sources.cors_for_maplibre: Yes, checked 18 November 2026 from http://127.0.0.1:8080: Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflects the request Origin; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true. Query and exportImage both returned those headers.
sources.notes: DateCurrent is a year. The app queries the latest sheet at or before the case year at the named-site point, then mosaics DateCurrent <= case year. At Aguadilla the latest sheet before 2013 is DateCurrent/Date_On_Map 1960, 1:20,000, imprint year 1983.

sources.name: USGS The National Map historic MapServer
sources.license: If the service existed, USGS National Map services are public domain with USGS credit.
sources.cors_for_maplibre: [UNKNOWN] — the service itself returned 404 Service historic/MapServer not found on 18 November 2026.
sources.notes: A third-party 2026 blog still lists this URL. It is not date-filterable even when present, so it would not be used as a dated period match.

sources.name: USGS EROS historical aerial photography
sources.coverage_years: About 1937–2014 for Aerial Photo Single Frames / mosaics (as published on the EROS collection page)
sources.coverage_regions: United States, sporadic, not a seamless nationwide mosaic
sources.tile_url: [UNKNOWN] — no public keyless XYZ or WMTS was found on USGS EROS itself. Access is through EarthExplorer, which requires a login for download.
sources.key_required: EarthExplorer account for download; no public tile key was found because no public tile API was found.
sources.license: U.S. Government work, generally public domain, with USGS credit. Confirm per frame if needed.
sources.notes: University of Montana Landscape Explorer offers a WMTS of mid-century EROS-derived imagery for 17 western U.S. states, but it is CC BY-NC 4.0, which is not used here.

sources.name: Esri World Imagery Wayback
sources.coverage_years: Release catalog 20 February 2014 through 29 October 2026 (198 releases checked in waybackconfig.json)
sources.coverage_regions: Worldwide mosaic; local update dates vary and can lag the release date
sources.license: Esri Master Agreement / Terms of Use, not a public-domain or CC license. Attribution required. The official Wayback app documents an ArcGIS APP_ID for its own client.
sources.cors_for_maplibre: Yes, checked 18 November 2026: tiles and the catalog JSON return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
sources.notes: Technically keyless and CORS-friendly, but not used: the license is not a free reuse grant, and the archive starts in 2014, which is after both current pilot dates (1980 and April 2013) if the rule is at or before the case date.

sources.name: National Library of Scotland Historic Maps API (MapTiler Cloud)
sources.coverage_regions: Great Britain, Ireland, and selected city layers
sources.license: Attribution to the National Library of Scotland required, plus MapTiler Cloud terms. Free tier is limited and non-commercial.
sources.cors_for_maplibre: [UNKNOWN] — not tested, because a key is required and keys are not used.
sources.notes: This API moved to MapTiler Cloud in March 2022 and is not keyless.

sources.name: NLS OS 1:2,500 National Grid, 1974 (hosted XYZ)
sources.coverage_years: 1974 (layer name/year; per-sheet survey dates inside the layer were not retrieved)
sources.coverage_regions: Great Britain; confirmed present at Rendlesham Forest / MOD Woodbridge at zooms 12–18 on 18 November 2026
sources.license: CC BY. Required credit: Courtesy of the National Library of Scotland. NLS also publishes a commercial reuse charging policy for high-volume use of its hosted georeferenced layers.
sources.notes: Used for Great Britain cases when the case date is 1974 or later and no closer dated source is available. Preferred over the 1949–1970 six-inch layer when both apply. App requests only zooms 12–18 and the Great Britain bounds, to avoid tile 404s.

sources.name: NLS OS 1:10,560 Great Britain, 1949–1970 (S3 XYZ)
sources.coverage_regions: Great Britain; confirmed at Rendlesham at zooms 12–16; zoom 18 was 404
sources.license: CC BY. Courtesy of the National Library of Scotland.
sources.cors_for_maplibre: Yes, S3 tiles return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (checked on neighboring NLS S3 tilesets, 18 November 2026).
sources.notes: Fallback for Great Britain when the case date is before 1974 and at or after 1949, or if a later NLS layer does not apply. App requests only zooms 12–16 and the Great Britain bounds, to avoid tile 404s.

sources.name: OpenHistoricalMap vector tiles
sources.coverage_years: Features are individually dated; coverage is worldwide but sparse and uneven
sources.coverage_regions: Worldwide, only where contributors have mapped a dated feature
sources.license: Data is generally CC0 / public domain unless a feature is tagged otherwise. Landmass tiles derived from OpenStreetMap coastlines are ODbL. Courtesy credit to OpenHistoricalMap is requested.
sources.cors_for_maplibre: Yes, checked 18 November 2026: vtiles and the unpkg style JSON return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. A Rendlesham z14 tile was HTTP 204 (empty), which is expected where no features are present.
sources.notes: Used only as a dated overlay of buildings and roads (start_decdate / end_decdate). Features without a start date are hidden so undated data is not presented as period-correct. The overlay is never the sole basis for a Period map label.
